issues.description: Removed `public` API surface (NAME, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval) without a deprecation cycle
issues.detail: These were public constants/methods on a previously-released format class. Demoting them to package-private in the same release that relocates the class is a hard ABI break for anyone touching them by name. If the class is now legacy, leave the symbols public-and-deprecated for one cycle, then remove. Otherwise external code that reads old segments via these symbols breaks at link time.

issues.description: fieldsWriter() throws UnsupportedOperationException but the no-arg public constructor still exists and is registered via SPI
issues.detail: A user who instantiates `new Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat()` (still public, SPI-listed) gets a perfectly happy object that explodes only at write time. That is the wrong failure point. Either remove the public constructors entirely, or throw from the ctor with a message pointing at Lucene104. Bombing inside fieldsWriter wastes a maintainer's afternoon debugging an indexer.

issues.description: Patch does three things at once: relocate, narrow visibility, and disable write path
issues.detail: This should have been three commits. Move-only (no semantic change) is a trivial review. Visibility narrowing is an API decision. Disabling writes is a behavior change. Squashing them makes the diff misleading: `similarity index 91/92/98%` hides real semantic changes inside what looks like a rename. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: Protected fields on OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues silently demoted to package-private
issues.detail: The class is still `public abstract`, so external subclasses existed in theory. Changing `protected` to package-private breaks any subclass outside the package without a compile error message that explains why. If this is intentional because the class should never have been subclassable externally, mark the class final or seal it; don't quietly strip access modifiers.

issues.description: Dead fields numMergeWorkers/mergeExec removed but constructor still accepts and validates them
issues.detail: The constructor still takes `numMergeWorkers` and `mergeExec`, runs the executor null-check, then discards both. That is a lie in the API: the parameters do nothing. Since the writer now throws anyway, either drop the parameters from the ctor or document that they are accepted only for source-compat and ignored. Right now it reads like a half-done refactor.

issues.description: Test scaffolding Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat duplicates production constructor logic
issues.detail: The RW test subclass re-exposes the writer by overriding fieldsWriter. Fine. But it relies on package-private `rawVectorFormat`, `flatVectorScorer`, `confidenceInterval`, `bits`, `compress` reaching across from the moved class. That coupling is the reason the visibility was narrowed in a confusing way. A cleaner shape: keep a protected hook `createWriter()` on the production class, override in tests. Smaller surface, no test-driven access leakage.

review.summary: Patch is the right direction — legacy formats belong in backward_codecs and writes should be refused — but the diff conflates a move, a visibility narrowing, and a behavior change, which makes the `similarity index 9x%` headers hide the real edits. NEEDS-WORK on two fronts: the public-to-package-private demotion of NAME/QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT/calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval is an undeclared ABI break in the same release as the relocation, and the writer now throws at use-time while the public no-arg constructor and SPI registration still happily hand out instances — fail at construction, not at the first index flush. Split into three patches: pure move, visibility/deprecation, write-disable. Then this lands.
